messages:
alex: Heads-up — noticed some requests to /v1/internal/* are getting the user Authorization header stripped in the gateway rewrite stage. Happened after the recent header-normalizer change.
jamie: Ugh. Is that the new canonicalize-headers step? Which header exactly is being removed?
alex: The whole `Authorization` header is gone for proxied internal routes. External routes look fine.
priya: Any logs from the rewrite plugin? Could be a rule with `remove_headers: ["authorization"]` applied to a route match that shouldn't.
alex: I pulled the envoy config dump. Here's the relevant snippet we see applied to the route:
```
- match: { prefix: "/v1/" }
  rewrite:
    path_prefix: "/"
    remove_request_headers: ["Authorization"]
```
matt: That looks like a legacy rule we used to strip user tokens on public-facing buckets. It must have been grafted onto the prefix match too broadly.
jamie: Why would remove_request_headers be on prefix /v1/? That's aggressive.
priya: We used to strip Authorization for the static asset routes under `/v1/static` only. Maybe the rule lost a more specific `match` after the normalize pass collapsed `/v1/static -> /v1/`.
infra-bot: deploy-bot reported a canary of header-normalizer v2 at 1795599000 completed (10% traffic). No rollback.
deploy-bot: Canary notes: "normalize-headers: collapse-case, drop-empty, dedupe". No intention to remove Authorization.
alex: I reproduced locally: when header-normalizer lowercases header names, a later rule that matches `authorization` vs `Authorization` did not hit, so the broader rule executed and dropped header.
jamie: So case normalization changed internal routing for the rewrite plugin because rules are case-sensitive. Great.
priya: Fix options:
- Make header removal rules case-insensitive matcher (preferred)
- Re-scope the remove rule to `/v1/static` explicit
- Update ordering so explicit routes run before prefix fallback
jamie: We should avoid brittle case sensitivity in matchers. Can we change the gateway to treat header names canonicalized consistently at rule-compile time?
matt: Quick patch: add `match_normalized_headers: true` flag to the rewrite plugin and recompile. Minimal risky change.
priya: Also add unit tests for consolidated header-normalizer + rewrite interaction (simulate lowercase/uppercase).
alex: For the immediate customer impact: can we push a targeted revert so internal `/v1/internal/*` calls keep Authorization? I can add an explicit `add_request_headers: ["Authorization"]` fallback but that's ugly.
jamie: Don't re-add tokens. Instead scope the existing remove rule to an exact path. I'll open a hotfix PR with revert of the normalization that affected header match ordering and a single-route patch.
priya: Suggestion for long-term: switch rewrite rules to operate on a canonical header key vector (lowercased internally) and store rule definitions normalized at config-load. That avoids order-dependence.
alex: Agreed. Also we should emit telemetry when a rule removes an auth header — bucket by route and rule id. That would have flagged this in canary.
matt: I'll add a metric: `gateway.rewrite.headers_removed{header="authorization",route="..."}`. Low overhead.
infra-bot: Created issue #INF-432: "gateway: header-normalizer + rewrite ordering causes auth header removal for internal routes". Assigned to eng-platform.
jamie: For the canary rollback — ops, we already rolled forward to 50%. Stop that and revert to 5% until fix is out.
deploy-bot: Rolling canary back to 5% at 1795601100 — initiated.
alex: After the revert, I re-tested and Authorization is preserved. Can we follow up with a small RFC describing canonicalization and rule compilation? Want to include examples for path normalization, query rewrites, header-case mapping, and precedence.
priya: I'll draft the RFC. Will propose these invariants:
- All header matching is done on lowercased header names.
- Route match specificity: exact > prefix > regex > fallback.
- Rewrite rules are applied in route-specific order; global rewrites last.
- Any rule that removes `authorization` must include an allowlist of target hosts or explicit path.
matt: Add acceptance test that runs a matrix of header cases and ensures no token loss.
jamie: Thanks all. Alex — can you paste a minimal reproduce script (curl) here so support can triage affected calls?
alex: Yep:
```
# reproducer
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer XXX" "https://gateway.example.com/v1/internal/health"
# expected: 200 and backend sees Authorization header
# observed: 200 but backend logged no Authorization
```
priya: Copying that into the hotfix PR.
jamie: :thumbsup: moving to follow-ups — RFC + metric + unit tests + hotfix PR. Keep the thread updated.
infra-bot: INF-432 updated: PR 2175 attached, deploy rollback executed.
matt: I'll own the metric & tests. Priya you'll own the RFC? Jamie you do the hotfix PR?
priya: Yup.
alex: Thanks team. Will monitor logs for the next hour.
jamie: Closing loop — if anyone sees regression ping #oncall and me.
